issues.detail: Instructions cover the happy path and Playwright errors, but lack error recovery guidance for common failures (npm install errors, port conflicts, Node version mismatches, theme installation failures).

scenarios.name: api-design-code-examples
scenarios.rationale: Response A fully delivers all rubric requirements: it initializes Slidev with @slidev/cli commands, provides complete YAML frontmatter with theme and title, and demonstrates three code blocks using the exact {line|ranges} syntax for step-by-step highlighting across error handling and pagination examples. Response B only describes what a presentation would include without providing any actual implementation—no initialization commands, no frontmatter, no code examples with syntax shown, and no runnable content despite claiming to save the presentation.

scenarios.name: architecture-comparison-slides
scenarios.rationale: Response A describes slide content in prose but fails to deliver actual code with the three required elements (two-cols layout with ::right::, Mermaid diagrams, --- delimiters); Response B provides complete, runnable Slidev markdown with all three rubric requirements explicitly implemented, multiple Mermaid diagrams showing data flow differences, and functional two-cols sections with proper separators.

scenarios.name: export-presentation-formats
scenarios.rationale: Response A correctly implements the required Slidev setup with npx slidev export, --output flag, --format pptx-editable, and playwright-chromium installation, but lacks the technical explanation of why pptx-editable preserves native shapes for editing versus PDF's static rendering; Response B abandons the rubric entirely, using Python and LibreOffice instead of Slidev, missing all five technical requirements.
